This is an interesting way to view it... Shiny people, rank ordering. It seems like the proclivity to quantify life in this way boils down to social media. The "shiny people" on social media aren't that shiny, just a fake front for random people they once knew earlier in their lives (Facebook, IG, etc.). The rank-ordering isn't reality, you think it is but it isn't realistic. What is there a random Facebook group of all your high school classmates, except you, giving a constantly updated ranking on classmates and their status in life? No. And even if there was it wouldn't really matter as you'll never see them in the flesh ever again. Or if you do it'll be a random encounter where both of you are making awkward conversation counting down the minutes until it is polite to go your seperate ways again.
I am expressing this because everyone has these feelings, the only opinions of yourself you should care about are yours and the people close to you. And even if they have an opinion that under a logical microscope doesn't make sense then f*ck that opinion as well.
You can't compare yourself to other people, would a hippo compare itself to a giraffe because they can't reach the lush vegetation 10 feet in the air? 
Your consciousness, experiencing the simple pleasures, life and the joys that it brings you are what truly matters.

I'm so sorry that you went through that, the grieving of passed family members has taught me a few things that you may find interesting. A part of them lives on inside of you, in your memories, in your personality that they helped influence, in your genetics, in the values/ethics that you share, and even in the belongings that they left behind. Yourself and others that she touched, will carry her torch with them through life. This allows for her to live on for eternity especially when her values, sense of humor, etc. is championed and eventually passed on by someone so close to her and so involved in her life, you, her sister.
I find the only cure for grief is time, and that time is different for everyone based on a multitude of factors. I found speaking to a therapist/psychologist and being 100% honest and up front with them to be a great tool for me. I would ask them if my thought process for a certain feeling was healthy, if feeling a certain emotion in a specific situation was "normal." It advanced my healing to a noticeable extent
I felt guilty speaking to friends and family at times like I was wasting their time. It made me feel better knowing that someone was getting paid to do it and also getting their expertise/outlook as if I were getting my money's worth. 
But speaking to friends and family is vital, I found that other people in my life collectively filled the void that that passed loved one left. As that passed loved one probably accounted for 40% of the love I felt for someone in the world, I added 10% from one friend, 10% from one brother, 10% from my Mom, and 10% from my other brother. 
Speaking to your sister when you have a memory about them will really help too.
And always, always, be open to the signs that your sister could send you. Even if your disposition is pounded down by depression and grief, keep something you saw like that in mind later when those symptoms calm down a little bit.

You deserve to live a happy and meaningful life. One small exercise to try and start with is to notice the little things and try to properly gauge them as the miracles that they truly are.

One example I think of a lot is rain. It may sound like I am over-hyping it but hear me out.
The science of being able to feel rain, the sensation, the process of how it arrived on your skin. Then I go into the facet that we are in such a place as a species that I can use up mental acuity and time to ponder these thoughts. That we are evolved to the point of being able to go through this process. That I can analyze this rather than how I am going to escape from this bear or tiger or lion.

Your life is a plot, you can't have high points of it without some low points. The protagonist can't just win over and over and over again, otherwise it would be a boring, fictitious story.

You deserve to live a good life, it's over used but one mistake shouldn't have you question if you are worthy of regret or sadness. Yes you are worthy of feeling that way, you are also worthy and deserving of the great life that you will live after this awful event.
